text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P-45321 triggered for service=inference-api — elevated 5xx rate observed in us-west-1c. ELB target health is flapping, Route53 health checks returning unhealthy. Auto-scaling not helping right now.

alice: seeing this on dashboards — 5xx from 17:02 UTC, 40-60% of requests failing to pods behind elb/us-west-1c. Error is `HTTP 502` and `TARGET_UNHEALTHY` in the ELB console.

bob: pulling logs now. CPU/mem on hosts look fine. getting repeated connection reset / TCP timeout in ELB logs.

sre-ken: I’m taking lead. tagging in networking-liz. can someone pause any noncritical deploys to that AZ?

networking-liz: paused. Looking at aws console — Route53 health checks for the regional failover are flapping between PASS/FAIL. ELB target groups show many "initial"/"unused" states.

ops-maya: paging history shows a related flapping event earlier but short-lived. This one started at 17:02 and sustained.

bob: quick customer impact check — sampling 10k requests in 17:05–17:08: 18% 5xx, p50 latency up 3x. A handful of enterprise customers are seeing errors.

product-jess: heads-up — two paying customers (acct: AC-442, AC-991) reported degraded behavior. We should prepare a status update.

sre-ken: mitigation plan: 1) reduce Route53 TTL to 30s; 2) shift 70% of weighted traffic away from us-west-1c to us-east-1; 3) drain ELB targets in problematic AZ to allow healthy nodes to serve; 4) abort any recent infra changes.

alice: lowering TTL now. running:
```
# lower global RRset TTL for inference endpoint
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.example.com","Type":"A","TTL":30,"SetIdentifier":"us-west-1","Weight":10,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"34.12.45.66"}]}}]}'
```

networking-liz: applying weighted failover. pushing weight 70 -> us-east-1. sending change to Route53:
```
# change-batch snippet (abbreviated)
{
  "Changes": [
    {"Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "inference.redwood.example.com", "Type": "A", "SetIdentifier": "us-west-1c", "Weight": 10 }},
    {"Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "inference.redwood.example.com", "Type": "A", "SetIdentifier": "us-east-1", "Weight": 90 }}
  ]
}
```

bob: started deregistering targets in target-group arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-1:111111:targetgroup/tg-inference-1/abcd1234 — draining 6/12 targets.

sre-ken: confirm health checks — we want to avoid cascading deregistration. do graceful drain with 300s connection termination.

ops-maya: updated PagerDuty with mitigation steps and current status. Notified on-call rotation for possible escalation.

alice: after initial weight shift p50 latency for remaining us-west-1c requests dropped a bit but overall error rate decreased to ~6% within 90s. Good signal.

product-jess: drafted status page message: "We are investigating elevated errors impacting inference API in US-WEST-1. Traffic is being shifted to a healthy region; short-term mitigation underway." Want to publish?

sre-ken: publish now. include ETA: 30m for full recovery and mention impacted customers will be contacted directly.

networking-liz: digging into why health-checks flapped — seeing periodic TCP RSTs from ENIs in us-west-1c. Opening a ticket with AWS (case 1234567890).

bob: stack trace sample from node showing connection resets:
```
[17:04:12] net/http: read tcp 10.0.5.23:443->10.0.8.45:54012: read: connection reset by peer
[17:04:12] elb: target unhealthy (timeout)
```

ops-maya: customer-impact tally: approx 120k requests failed in first 6 minutes, ~0.9% of daily volume. High concentration from US clients routed to us-west-1c.

sre-ken: escalate if AWS doesn't respond in 10m. Meanwhile keep weighted routing in place until we have stable healthchecks for >5m.

networking-liz: AWS support acknowledged and asked for ELB control-plane logs — sending now. AWS noted potential networking fabric instability in AZ c, recommended traffic shift.

alice: monitoring shows complete drop to 1% 5xx after 10m. Rolling window looks stable.

product-jess: PRD notify sent to AC-442 & AC-991 with interim mitigation details and offer to open support calls.

sre-ken: ops checklist before closing: 1) confirm AWS case updates and root cause; 2) reintroduce targets slowly once control plane fixed; 3) restore original Route53 weights and TTL (set back to 300); 4) run post-incident eval and blameless postmortem.

ops-maya: creating incident doc and assigning to oncall-sm for postmortem.

networking-liz: AWS replied — they saw control-plane retries in that AZ; working a broader networking remediation. They estimate 45m for full stabilization.

bob: scheduling a canary re-add of drained targets in 20m once AWS confirms.

sre-ken: handoff note for next on-call: track AWS case #1234567890, keep Route53 weights at failover values until AWS confirms stable health for 10m, and coordinate customer comms if recovery slips past 45m.

product-jess: thanks everyone — will follow up with customers and ops doc. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P-45321 updated: status=mitigated, note="Traffic shifted from us-west-1c to us-east-1; targets drained; AWS case opened (1234567890). Postmortem required."
